name: THE FRIENDLY NEIGHBORHOOD
message:
Take a picture and transform it into a warm, gentle scene from the original, beloved children's television program, Mr. Rogers' Neighborhood, in the tradition of the quiet, unhurried neighborhood-host shows of the 1960s-1980s. Place the subject as a warm, invented neighborhood host figure — cardigan sweater being buttoned or already on, sneakers being changed at the door, a soft-spoken, unhurried demeanor — welcoming the viewer into a cozy, handmade television set built from warm wood tones, painted backdrops, and practical household props, NOT a specific existing published or broadcast show's exact set design, characters, or puppets.

ADDITIONAL INSTRUCTIONS
This must read as a lovingly-made ORIGINAL production — invent your own distinct sweater pattern/color, your own trolley-adjacent or vehicle-adjacent transition device if included, and your own puppet/neighbor characters with clearly different names, designs, and personalities from any existing real program. The overall feeling should be warmth, patience, and unconditional kindness — a slower pace than modern children's television, direct warm eye contact with the camera, simple honest language implied through gentle expression.

NEGATIVE PROMPT
fast cuts, frantic pacing, flashy CGI, modern smartphone-era production values, cynicism, sarcasm, loud aggressive colors, corporate slickness, any specific real broadcast show's exact character names, puppet designs, set layout, or branding.

RANDOMIZATION RECOMMENDATION
Yes. Mixing the specific WARMTH_MOMENT beats with the specific SET_DETAIL treatments produces a wide, varied set of cozy scenes while keeping the entire preset anchored to one consistent, original gentle-neighborhood identity.

CREATIVE STRATEGY
This preset uses two internal variable axes merged into one flat options list per the app's schema: options 001-010 are WARMTH_MOMENT (the specific gentle beat being depicted), and options 011-020 are SET_DETAIL (the specific practical, handmade production texture). The fixed, unchanging parameters are the cardigan-and-sneakers ritual, the unhurried pace, and the original-character rule. The variables are the specific moment and the specific set texture layered on top of that fixed identity.

VISUAL DNA ANALYSIS
Cinematic Identity: Warm public-television children's programming — soft 16mm-adjacent broadcast texture, not slick modern video.
Atmosphere: Calm, patient, unconditionally kind, unhurried.
Framing Tendencies: Static or slow-pan camera, direct-address medium shots, warm practical lighting.
Emotional Tone: Safety, gentleness, being truly listened to.
Material Language: Knit wool, varnished wood, painted matte backdrops, felt and yarn puppet textures, soft incandescent light.
Color Relationships: Warm mustard, forest green, and rust tones against soft cream backgrounds, gentle and never garish.
Visual Storytelling: Slowness and ritual — the simple act of changing shoes or buttoning a sweater is itself the story, not a transition to skip past.

name: TECHNICOLOR GOLDEN AGE GLAMOUR PORTRAIT
message:
Take a picture and transform it into a lush, saturated 1950s Hollywood studio portrait in the style of classic three-strip Technicolor cinematography, while preserving the subject's identity exactly. Create the feeling of a glamorous studio publicity still — the kind shot on a soundstage for a major star under contract to a golden-age studio.

Composition: Tight head-and-shoulders or mid-torso portrait, subject fills most of the frame, direct or subtly angled eye contact with the camera, a poised, deliberately glamorous pose. The final image should feel intentional, theatrical, and richly colored — every element of light, pose, expression, and color grading working together as a single coherent studio-glamour decision, not a filter applied over a snapshot.

ADDITIONAL INSTRUCTIONS
Subject's facial identity, proportions, and recognizable features must be preserved exactly — this is a lighting, pose, expression, and color-grading transformation, not a reimagining of the person. Skin tones should be smooth and luminous in the flattering studio-glamour tradition, but must retain natural texture rather than becoming plastic or artificial. Wardrobe and hair styling should read as period-appropriate 1950s glamour (curled or waved hairstyles, fabric drapes, gloves, pearls) adapted naturally from whatever the subject is wearing. Background should remain a simple, elegant studio backdrop or soft color wash so all visual weight stays on the face, light, and color.

NEGATIVE PROMPT
desaturated, black and white, modern casual clothing, cluttered or busy background, harsh digital sharpening halos, plastic overly-smoothed skin, snapshot-casual framing, wide-angle distortion, contemporary makeup trends, visible logos or branding, low resolution, amateur flash photography, muted or naturalistic color grading.

RANDOMIZATION RECOMMENDATION
Yes. Randomizing one selection from each of the four groups (Lighting, Pose, Expression, Color Palette) independently produces thousands of coherent, non-contradictory Technicolor-glamour variations, since each group governs a genuinely separate technical or performative axis of the image rather than overlapping with the others.

CREATIVE STRATEGY
Four internal variable axes, flattened into one options list per the app's actual schema: options 001–010 are LIGHTING (the physical light setup), 011–020 are POSE (body/head positioning), 021–030 are EXPRESSION (the emotional register of the face), and 031–040 are COLOR_PALETTE (the specific Technicolor grading treatment, replacing the prior preset's film-grain axis since color, not print texture, is the defining character here). The fixed, unchanging parameters are strict identity preservation, rich saturated Technicolor output, and tight glamour-studio framing. The variables are how the subject is lit, how they're positioned, what they're feeling, and which specific saturated color language dominates the frame.

VISUAL DNA ANALYSIS
Cinematic Identity: Golden-age studio publicity photography — the visual language of a contract star's official studio portrait, evoking the era without replicating any specific real actor's likeness or a specific copyrighted film still.
Atmosphere: Theatrical, luminous, larger-than-life, glamorous.
Framing Tendencies: Tight, frame-filling, classically posed, symmetrical or gracefully asymmetrical.
Emotional Tone: Ranges from radiant warmth to sultry allure to dramatic intensity, always polished and performative.
Material Language: Satin and velvet drapes, curled and waved hair, pearls and gloves, soft diffused studio light, glossy skin luminosity.
Color Relationships: Heightened, saturated primaries — ruby reds, jewel-tone blues and greens, warm golden skin tones — carrying the same emotional weight that pure black-and-white tonal range carried in the prior preset.
Visual Storytelling: Color itself as spectacle — the specific post-war thrill of seeing a face rendered in impossibly rich, dreamlike Technicolor for the first time.

Randomizing one selection from each of the four groups (Lighting, Pose, Expression, Film Texture) independently produces thousands of coherent, non-contradictory Sunset Strip Polaroid variations, since each group governs a genuinely separate technical or performative axis of the image rather than overlapping with the others.

name: RICHARD SIMMONS RETRO FITNESS LEGEND
message: Take a picture and transform it into an explosive, ultra-vibrant 1980s aerobics aesthetic inspired by the iconic career and flamboyant energy of Richard Simmons. CORE TRANSFORMATION: Convert the subject into a high-energy fitness personality or participant on a brightly lit studio floor or exercise class stage. Replace contemporary attire with classic 1980s activewear, including glittery dolphin shorts, tank tops, striped tube socks, and plush terrycloth wristbands. IDENTITY PRESERVATION: Maintain the subject's fundamental facial structure, ethnicity, and recognizable traits while adapting their posture into an expressive, joyful, and dynamic exercise pose. COMPOSITION: Framed in full-body or dynamic mid-shot, capturing wide studio depth with backing dancers or workout class participants in soft focus. ADDITIONAL INSTRUCTIONS: Utilize bright broadcast-television lighting, hyper-saturated color grading with magenta, teal, and electric yellow tones, and mild 1980s VHS tape texture with subtle scanlines. NEGATIVE PROMPTS: Moody lighting, minimalist modern gym equipment, dark shadows, muted colors, serious expressions, modern smartphone photography. RANDOMIZATION RECOMMENDATIONS: Combine varied studio backdrops (1980s TV set vs. Beverly Hills Slimmons style) with different energetic exercise actions. CREATIVE STRATEGY: Celebrate the theatrical, compassionate, and exuberantly joyful spirit of retro fitness culture. VISUAL DNA: High-energy 1980s broadcast video style, sparkling activewear, warm pastel studio gradients, and uninhibited theatrical emotion.
